name: Milesian School
description: Material monists searching for the primary substrate (arche) of the cosmos.

name: Eleatic School
description: Parmenidean metaphysics of immutable, indivisible Being and the illusion of change.

name: Ancient Atomism
description: Democritus and Leucippus: the universe consists entirely of indivisible atoms moving through the void.

name: Platonism
description: Dualistic metaphysics of immaterial, immutable Forms contrasted with the sensory realm of shadows.

name: Aristotelianism
description: Empirical naturalism, hylomorphism (matter and form), teleology, and virtue ethics.

name: Stoicism
description: Virtue as the sole good, living in accordance with Nature/Logos, and mastering inner impressions.

name: Epicureanism
description: Hedonism refined: pleasure as the absence of pain and mental anxiety (ataraxia).

name: Pyrrhonian Skepticism
description: Epoché (suspension of judgment) as the royal road to unshakeable tranquility.

name: Neoplatonism
description: Hierarchical emanation from the ineffable 'One' through Nous and Soul down to material existence.

name: Eastern Non-Dualism & Dao
description: Buddhism, Daoism, and Advaita Vedanta exploring the nature of consciousness, emptiness, and harmony.

name: Scholasticism
description: Methodical synthesis of Christian revelation with Aristotelian logic and metaphysics.

name: Falsafa (Islamic Philosophy)
description: Ibn Sina, Al-Farabi, and Ibn Rushd preserving, expanding, and refining Hellenistic philosophy.

name: Continental Rationalism
description: Intellectual intuition and deduction from innate ideas as the primary source of knowledge (Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz).

name: British Empiricism
description: All knowledge originates in sensory experience (Locke, Berkeley, Hume).

name: Social Contract & Enlightenment
description: Political legitimacy derived from the governed; human autonomy and critique of prejudice.

name: German Idealism
description: Transcendental idealism (Kant) and Absolute Idealism (Hegel): mind constructing reality.

name: 19th c. Existential & Radical Thought
description: Critique of grand systematic philosophy; focus on individual passion, alienation, and will.

name: Utilitarianism
description: Consequentialist ethics maximizing happiness and minimizing suffering for the greatest number.

name: American Pragmatism
description: The meaning and truth of an idea reside in its practical, experiential consequences.

name: Phenomenology
description: Direct investigation of conscious experience and structures of phenomena 'to the things themselves'.

name: Existentialism
description: Existence precedes essence: radical freedom, anxiety, bad faith, and the creation of personal meaning.

name: Analytic Philosophy & Logic
description: Conceptual clarification through formal logic, linguistics, and critique of metaphysical pseudo-problems.

name: Frankfurt School & Critical Theory
description: Critique of modern rationalization, cultural commodification, and capitalist alienation.

name: Structuralism & Semiotics
description: Analysis of culture, language, and meaning as relational systems of signs, binary oppositions, and differential structures.

name: Post-Structuralism & Contemporary
description: Decentering the subject, deconstruction of binary hierarchies, surveillance, biopolitics, and simulation.

name: Experimental Psychology
description: Wilhelm Wundt's scientific introspection, reaction times, and voluntarist structural analysis of conscious experience.

name: Psychoanalysis & Depth Psychology
description: Freud and Jung: the dynamic unconscious, repression, dream work, archetypes, and the psyche.

name: Behaviorism
description: Pavlov, Watson, and Skinner: organismic stimulus-response conditioning, reinforcement schedules, and rejection of mentalist assumptions.

name: Genetic Epistemology & Development
description: Piaget and Vygotsky: construction of cognitive schemas, developmental stages, and social mediation.

name: Cognitive Revolution
description: Information processing, Chomskyan innate generative grammar, and computational models of mind.

name: Humanistic & Existential Psychology
description: Carl Rogers, Maslow, and Frankl: self-actualization, phenomenology of experience, and the will to meaning.

name: Behavioral Decision Research
description: Kahneman and Tversky: cognitive biases, heuristics, System 1 and System 2 dual-process theory, and prospect theory.

name: Classical Positivism & Social Physics
description: Auguste Comte: empirical laws of human society, law of the three stages, and the birth of sociology.

name: Structural Functionalism
description: Durkheim and Parsons: sui generis social facts, collective conscience, anomie, and system integration.

name: Interpretive Sociology (Verstehen)
description: Max Weber: meaningful social action, the Protestant ethic, rationalization, and the iron cage of modern bureaucracy.

name: Formal Sociology & Urban Ecology
description: Georg Simmel: geometries of social interaction, the stranger, money economy, and psychological tensions of metropolitan life.

name: Symbolic Interactionism & Dramaturgy
description: G.H. Mead and Erving Goffman: emergence of self through symbolic interaction, the generalized other, and impression management.

name: Kyoto School & Modern Asian Thought
description: Nishida, Nishitani, and Watsuji: synthesis of Zen Buddhist ontology with Continental phenomenology and existentialism.

name: Africana & African Philosophy
description: Ptahhotep, Zara Yaqob, Amo, Césaire, Wiredu, and Mbembe: classical moral inquiry, Ethiopian rationalism, anti-colonial critique, conceptual decolonization, and necropolitics.

name: Latin American & Decolonial Philosophy
description: Sor Juana, Freire, Dussel, Quijano, and Anzaldúa: philosophy of liberation, critical consciousness, coloniality of power, and borderland epistemology.

name: Double Consciousness & Critical Sociology
description: W.E.B. Du Bois: sociological inquiry into the color line, the veil, and racial capitalism.

name: Indigenous & First Nations Philosophy
description: Nezahualcoyotl, Guaman Poma, Inca Garcilaso, Deloria, and Kimmerer: flower and song (in xochitl in cuicatl), Andean reciprocity (ayni), spatial metaphysics, and the grammar of animacy.

name: Genetic Structuralism & Field Theory
description: Pierre Bourdieu: embodied habitus, cultural/social capital, fields of power, and symbolic violence.

name: Late Modernity & Risk Society
description: Giddens, Bauman, and Beck: structuration, liquid modernity, reflexive modernization, and global risk regimes.
